367	## 9. Architecture decisions
368	
369	Short decision records, newest last. Add one when a change alters structure,
370	infrastructure, or a cross-cutting rule. Older, longer feature-level reasoning
371	is in [`specs/`](../specs/README.md).
372	
373	| # | Date | Decision | Why / consequences |
374	|---|---|---|---|
375	| D1 | 2026-01 | Phoenix LiveView monolith with phx.gen.auth scopes | One deployable, server-rendered real-time UI. All data is scoped per user. |
376	| D2 | 2026-03 | Persist every extraction attempt as a row; one review decision per extraction | Keeps history, and humans approve before booking. See `specs/001`, `specs/002`. |
377	| D3 | 2026-05 | Journal entries only from approved or amended decisions | AI never writes to the books directly. |
378	| D4 | 2026-06 | Kamal 2 on a single VPS, app reachable only over WireGuard | Low cost, private by default. Postgres runs as a Kamal accessory. |
379	| D5 | 2026-08 | Per-role LLM backends (extractor and verifier) selected by env, with no fallback | Models can be swapped or mixed (local and cloud) without code changes. Misconfiguration fails loudly. |
380	| D6 | 2026-08 | Document bytes in S3-compatible storage (self-hosted RustFS), with a provider-neutral `Storage` facade | Decouples bytes from the release. A later provider switch is config only. See `specs/003`. |
381	| D7 | 2026-09 | TypeSafe Jev as a *shadow* verifier | Collects independent per-field error probabilities without affecting outcomes until it is trusted. |
382	| D8 | 2026-09 | Replace fire-and-forget `Task` OCR with durable Oban jobs, enqueued in the upload transaction | Uploads can't lose their job. Retries, Lifeline rescue, user retry, and operator recovery. The TypeSafe shadow also moved to Oban. |
383	| D9 | 2026-10 | Add `stream_data` (test-only) for property-based tests on pure, boundary-heavy logic (currency normalization, error-retry classification, changeset validity, aggregation sums) | Generates and shrinks adversarial inputs instead of relying only on hand-picked examples; already caught an Ecto blank-string edge case in `Currency.normalize_and_validate/2`. DB-backed properties cap `max_runs` explicitly to bound CI time; `config :stream_data, max_runs` is lower locally, higher in CI (`CI=true`, set by GitHub Actions by default). |
384	| D10 | 2026-08 | Duplicate invoice detection: DB-enforced unique index, plus the journal entry in the same transaction as the review decision | A numbered invoice (same user, issuer, invoice number) cannot post twice; the database enforces it regardless of code path. An unnumbered exact `(issuer, date, amount, currency)` match warns and needs explicit confirmation. Posting the journal entry, tax claim, and event log now happens in the same `Ecto.Multi` as the decision update, so a duplicate or a failed audit write rolls the whole transition back — closing the gap in §11. |
385	| D11 | 2026-10 | Exact-byte SHA-256 fingerprints as an OCR-independent duplicate signal, copied to the journal entry at posting and enforced by a per-user partial unique index over unconfirmed postings | Re-uploading identical bytes is caught even when OCR/LLM reads different fields. A unique constraint cannot span document → extraction → review → entry, so the digest is snapshotted on the entry. Legitimately reused files (QR-bills, standing slips) post only with an explicit per-posting confirmation, recorded on the entry and in the event log. Legacy rows are filled by an online, idempotent backfill through the `Storage` facade, never by a migration. See `specs/004`. |
386	| D12 | 2026-10 | Upgrade to Elixir 1.20 (OTP unchanged at 28) | Elixir 1.20 completes zero-annotation type inference across all constructs, so the existing `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` CI gate now also catches unreachable clauses and dead code for free, no specs or Dialyzer required. Surfaced and removed 3 pre-existing dead branches (`review.ex`, `llm_client.ex`, `langfuse.ex`) that the 1.19 compiler couldn't see. First step toward the CI reliability work tracked for direct-to-main pushes; a complementary nightly Dialyzer job (whole-program success typing) is still planned separately. |
387	| D13 | 2026-10 | Split CI into `lint` / `test` / `security-audit` jobs; `mix credo --strict` and `mix hex.audit` run on every push but are advisory (non-blocking), with a separate nightly workflow re-running the audit so a CVE disclosed on a quiet day still gets caught | First step of hardening CI as the real safety net for pushing straight to `main` with less manual review. Credo and the audit aren't required checks yet because both already have a pre-existing backlog (51 Credo issues; `hackney` pinned to a vulnerable 1.x line by a test-only dependency) unrelated to any one change — see §11. `mix hex.audit` found 6 live advisories in locked dependencies; the `bandit` ones were fixed by a routine version bump in the same change, `hackney`'s needs a dependency change tracked separately. |
388	| D14 | 2026-10 | Add Dialyzer (dialyxir) as a nightly, advisory-only CI job rather than a required per-push check | Whole-program success typing complements the Elixir 1.20 compiler's own type inference (D12) by also checking across the OTP/dependency boundary, but PLT builds are too slow for a per-push gate. First run found 10 findings: 3 duplicated dead code already fixed by the Elixir 1.20 upgrade; 5 are a well-known Dialyzer/`Ecto.Multi` opaque-`MapSet` false positive; 2 (`storage/s3.ex`) are a `File.stream!/2` success-typing gap verified benign directly in `iex` before suppressing. All 7 non-duplicate false positives are listed individually in `.dialyzer_ignore.exs` with the reasoning, not blanket-ignored, so a genuinely new finding in the same file still surfaces. Also added missing `@type t :: %__MODULE__{}` to `ExtractedData` and `ExtractedContent.ExtractedContent` (matching the convention already used in `Document`/`ReviewDecision`), which cleared 9 separate `unknown_type` findings and makes every existing `@spec` referencing them actually checked going forward. |
389	| D15 | 2026-10 | Clear the 51-finding Credo backlog and make `mix credo --strict` blocking in the existing `lint` CI job | Supersedes D13's advisory Credo policy so new findings fail CI instead of rebuilding the backlog. Reorder aliases, alias nested module calls, use implicit function-level rescue/catch and readable string sigils, use `ReviewDecision.t()` in specs, and configure the existing TypeSafe Logger metadata explicitly. The two upload-test TODOs were stale: the same file already exercises uploads and edit submission, so replace them with references to that coverage. No checks are disabled and no findings are suppressed. Security audit and nightly Dialyzer remain advisory; GitHub branch protection settings are unchanged. |
390	| D16 | 2026-10 | Pin every workflow job to `runs-on: ubuntu-26.04` instead of `ubuntu-latest` | GitHub migrated the `ubuntu-latest` label from Ubuntu 24.04 to 26.04 gradually between October 19 and November 19, 2026, so two runs of the same commit could land on different images with no repo change. Pinning makes the toolchain that a green build was verified against explicit and reproducible, and turns the next image adoption into a deliberate commit rather than a silent rollover. `ubuntu-26.04` is GA on x64, and all five jobs only need Docker, the Postgres service container, and `erlef/setup-beam`'s Elixir/OTP builds, which the new image supports. |
391	| D17 | 2026-11 | One invoice page (`/documents/:id`) replaces the review, amend, and journal-entry posting screens, so it is the only place an entry is booked; checking and booking are one transaction. `/documents/:id/edit` remains and only replaces the stored file | The flow split one invoice over three pages that did not link to each other, so a treated or amended invoice was hard to find again. `Review.approve_invoice/4` and `amend_invoice/5` take `:booking` and `:tax_claim_attrs`, and `Accounting.create_multi_from_decision/3` posts the entry inside the existing review transaction, so a booking error rolls back the whole posting like a duplicate does. One comment per invoice (stored as review notes and copied to the entry's notes). Extraction feedback is sent automatically on posting so Langfuse gets a signal for every posted invoice. A rejection sends a score only when the user picked 👍/👎, because a correctly read duplicate is rejected too. |

defmodule ZaimuTomo.Release do
  @moduledoc """
  Release helpers used by deployment tasks.
  """

  @app :zaimu_tomo

  alias ZaimuTomo.Accounting.LegacyBookingBackfill
  alias ZaimuTomo.DocumentProcessing
  alias ZaimuTomo.Documents.FingerprintBackfill
  alias ZaimuTomo.Storage.{Migration, Verification}

  def migrate do
    load_app()

    for repo <- repos() do
      {:ok, _, _} = Ecto.Migrator.with_repo(repo, &Ecto.Migrator.run(&1, :up, all: true))
    end
  end

  def rollback(repo, version) do
    load_app()
    {:ok, _, _} = Ecto.Migrator.with_repo(repo, &Ecto.Migrator.run(&1, :down, to: version))
  end

  def migrate_to_s3!(source_dir) when is_binary(source_dir) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(Migration.migrate(source_dir), Migration)
  end

  def migrate_to_s3_from_env! do
    System.fetch_env!("SOURCE_DIR")
    |> migrate_to_s3!()
  end

  def backfill_document_fingerprints!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(FingerprintBackfill.run(opts), FingerprintBackfill)
  end

  def backfill_legacy_bookings!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(LegacyBookingBackfill.run(opts), LegacyBookingBackfill)
  end

  def verify_storage! do
    start_app()
    report_or_raise(Verification.verify(), Verification)
  end

  def recover_stuck_documents!(opts \\ []) do
    start_app()
    groups = DocumentProcessing.Recovery.list_stuck()
    Enum.each(groups, &print_stuck_group/1)

    dispatch_recovery(Keyword.get(opts, :confirm, false), groups)
  end

  defp dispatch_recovery(true, groups) do
    jobs = DocumentProcessing.Recovery.enqueue_stuck(groups)
    IO.puts("Enqueued #{length(jobs)} OCR jobs.")
    groups
  end

  defp dispatch_recovery(false, groups) do
    count = groups |> Enum.map(&length(&1.document_ids)) |> Enum.sum()
    IO.puts("Dry run: #{count} stuck documents — nothing enqueued.")
    IO.puts("Re-run with confirm: true (or CONFIRM=true) to enqueue.")
    groups
  end

  defp print_stuck_group(%{user_id: user_id, currency: currency, document_ids: document_ids}) do
    IO.puts("user #{user_id} (#{currency}): document ids #{Enum.join(document_ids, ", ")}")
  end

  defp repos do
    Application.fetch_env!(@app, :ecto_repos)
  end

  defp load_app do
    Application.load(@app)
  end

  defp start_app do
    load_app()

    # Eval nodes run maintenance only: no queues, no plugins, no leadership, so
    # a short-lived node never grabs a job and dies mid-run (leaving it orphaned
    # until Lifeline rescues it).
    oban = Application.fetch_env!(@app, Oban)

    Application.put_env(
      @app,
      Oban,
      Keyword.merge(oban, queues: false, plugins: false, peer: false)
    )

    case Application.ensure_all_started(@app) do
      {:ok, _started} -> :ok
      {:error, reason} -> raise "could not start #{@app}: #{inspect(reason)}"
    end
  end

  defp report_or_raise({status, summary}, formatter) do
    IO.puts(formatter.format_summary(summary))

    case status do
      :ok -> summary
      :error -> raise "maintenance command failed"
    end
  end
end

          {:ok, ExtractedContent.t()} | {:error, term()}
  def put_typesafe_shadow(extraction_id, shadow) when is_map(shadow) do
    case get_by_id(extraction_id) do
      %ExtractedContent{} = content ->
        analysis = content.analysis || %{}
        verification = Map.get(analysis, "verification", %{})

        updated_analysis =

        content
        |> Ecto.Changeset.change(analysis: updated_analysis)
        |> Repo.update()

    end
  end

**Comprehension review: /home/alexis/Development/private/zaimu-tomo/concepts_brief.md (Mode: BRAINSTORM)**

I read the persona, the full brief and the code the brief cites. The caller supplied no standards beyond the persona. Line numbers (L) refer to the brief. No files were written and no tests were run.

## Answers to your questions

**Could someone say what a user sees on "Audit log" for each kind of event?** No. The brief gives only four fragments of display text: "issuer, amount changed" (L280), "2 extractions, 1 review decision" (L300), "backfill updated 214 documents" (L152), and "Deleted user" (L323). It has no event catalogue, and even the row's name is contradictory (B1).

| Event kind | What the brief settles | What a reader cannot tell |
|---|---|---|
| Approve / book | Nothing specific | Whether it is one row or several; what names the invoice |
| Amend | Field names, no values (L280) | Whether booking values appear in the same row |
| Reject | Reason can be diffed (L281-282) | Whether the reason sits in `changes` or apart (L265-266) |
| Post / re-categorize | Category, need/want, notes | Tax-claim fields (status, deductible amount, tax year); the before state on first booking |
| File-reuse confirmed | Named only in staging (L342) | Whether it is covered (absent from L184-189) and what it displays |
| Upload, file replacement | "changes to documents" (L185) | Whether upload is an event; whether filename is diffed |
| Document delete | Child counts (L300) | Label, and the actor wording |
| Final extraction outcome | "error class only" (L188) | What "final" means; what success shows; what an error class looks like to a user |
| Recovery or Lifeline rescue | Named actor | Whether a rescue appears at all (M4) |
| Fingerprint backfill | Summary plus one row per document (L302-303) | Journal-entry changes; how rows collapse (B3, M6) |
| Legacy booking backfill | Not mentioned | Everything (M3) |
| Account create/update/delete | "account names" (L282) | Bank name, account number, type, currency |
| Balance snapshot | "balances" can be diffed | What a diff means for an insert-only row (M12) |
| Profile | Display name, base currency | Email and password changes (M11) |

**Does the Analysis still agree with the later decisions?** Partly. These parts no longer agree:
- §6 labels conflict with decision 2 (B1).
- §5's four job origins conflict with decision 6's three (M4).
- §1's "see Key Decisions" leads nowhere for migrations and seeds (M7).
- §7's page needs never reach Goals or Staging (M8).
- §6's format version is dropped (M13).
- §8 still talks about added columns (N2).
- The Overview still says the existing table is what gets upgraded (M1).

§2, §3 and §4 are reconciled with the decisions, apart from the stale facts in M2 and N3.

## Blockers

**B1. The entry label uses data that decision 2 bans**
- Severity: Blocker
- Location: L134-135 and L267, against L276-279; also L148 and L216
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: §6 says the write-time label is "a filename, or issuer and date", and the converging recommendation repeats the label. Decision 2 says issuer and date "never appear in the log, as values or as diffs". "Approved invoice X" (L216) and "names in place of ids" (L148) have no permitted source for X. Filename is the only surviving candidate, and decision 2's list does not mention it. It is also unclear whether the page may join the live issuer at read time. That would make a row's name change or vanish when its record is deleted.
- Ergonomic Requirement: State the exact label per subject type, and say whether read-time joins to extracted fields are allowed. Correct §6 and L267 to match.

**B2. There is no per-event definition of the page**
- Severity: Blocker
- Location: L144-153, L184-189, L274-283, L310-311
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: The page is the feature, but only its fields and filters are sketched. See the table above.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Add one table of event kinds with: trigger, actor shown, subject and label, fields shown, example row text, and link target.

**B3. "One event" is defined three incompatible ways**
- Severity: Blocker
- Location: L274-275, L302-304, L313-314, L188, L342
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction:
  - Criterion L313 requires "exactly one audit event" per covered write path.
  - Decision 5 writes 1 + N events for a backfill run.
  - L188 writes nothing for non-final extraction attempts, although each one is a write.
  - Since D17, one approve-and-book transaction writes `invoice_approved` and `journal_entry_posted`, plus `source_file_reuse_confirmed` when a reuse is confirmed. L341-342 still lists these separately, while decision 1 implies a single event.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Define the unit as the operation, list the deliberate exceptions, and state how many rows approve-and-book produces. Rewrite the criterion so it can be tested.

## Major

**M1. The Overview describes the rejected design**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L25, against L162-164, L248-251, L284-287
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: "This feature turns that table into a complete, user-readable history", but `event_logs` is frozen and replaced, with nothing copied. "Complete" also hides that the page has no pre-release history.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Rewrite L25, and specify the page's empty state or a "history starts on" notice.

**M2. Stale facts about the existing log**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L16-20, L60-61, L183; L341-342
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction:
  - L16 says four events, and L341-342 lists five. The code also has five, including `source_file_reuse_confirmed` (review.ex:402).
  - L17-20 and L60-61 call `post_entry` best-effort. It now writes its event inside the `Ecto.Multi` (accounting.ex:359), so only reject remains best-effort.
  - The reject write is at review.ex:101, not :96.
  - Goal L183, "the two paths", inherits the error.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Re-baseline these claims against the current branch.

**M3. The write-path inventory predates D17 and misses a writer**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L35, L54-55, L99-106, L184-189
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: L35 claims every write path was listed. `LegacyBookingBackfill` (/home/alexis/Development/private/zaimu-tomo/lib/zaimu_tomo/accounting/legacy_booking_backfill.ex, exposed at release.ex:41-44) is absent. It changes journal entries, writes `journal_entry_posted` events, and preserves `updated_at`. Its manual path calls `post_entry` with the entry's `user_id`, so the operator's run would look like the user's own action. The brief also never mentions D17's single booking flow.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Add this writer with a named actor, and redo the list against D17.

**M4. Actor identity is unresolved**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L118-123, L10, L305-309, L338
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction:
  - §5 lists four origins, and `initiated_by` has three values. Lifeline disappears without comment. A rescue re-runs the same job, so it would carry the original origin, but the brief never says that.
  - Key formats disagree: `system.ocr_job` against `Scope.system(:recovery)`.
  - For an upload, it is unclear whether the extraction's actor is the user or "document processing" (L10).
  - Old jobs defaulting to `upload` (L338) can misattribute recovery jobs.
  - L10 says "startup recovery", but release.ex:51 also exposes an operator-run recovery. It is unclear whether those two need different actors.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Provide a closed actor table with stable key, display label, and the rule for each origin. State that a rescue keeps the original actor, if that is the intent.

**M5. Owner of system events, and single-user versus per-user**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L65, L173, L234, against L181, L305-306, L317, L319
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: The brief argues from "single-user" but requires two-user isolation. `Scope.system(:fingerprint_backfill)` has no owner, and the backfill runs across all users. A per-run summary has no single owner, so it either leaks across users or disappears from the page.
- Ergonomic Requirement: State the tenancy model (single user in practice, per-user data model, if that is correct). Define how a system scope supplies the owner, for example one summary per affected user.

**M6. Decision 5 covers only half of the fingerprint backfill**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L41-44, L301-304, L182, L313-314
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: The backfill also sets `source_document_sha256` and `source_file_reuse_confirmed` on journal entries (fingerprint_backfill.ex:195). Decision 5 only speaks of documents. The reuse confirmation is a human decision made through a maintenance task, so its actor is unclear. A run-level summary also cannot share a transaction with row updates that commit one at a time, which conflicts with L182.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Specify the journal-entry events and the actor for confirmed reuse. Exempt the summary from the same-transaction rule explicitly, or define its transaction.

**M7. Migrations and dev seeds have no decision**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L50-56, against L299-304, L189, L313
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: L55-56 says these need explicit handling "(see Key Decisions)", but decision 5 covers only cascades and bulk updates. A silent migration is exactly the "trusted gap" L34-35 warns about.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Decide whether each is covered, excluded, or given an actor, and define "covered write path" accordingly.

**M8. §7's page requirements never become scope**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L142-153, against L180-181, L310-311, L339-340
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: Filters, keyset paging, label formatting and bulk collapse appear only as analysis. Decision 8 gives a name, but no route or navigation placement, although L142 says placement must keep the page distinct from Activity. Collapse has no run id or grouping key, and no stated default.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Move these items into Goals and specify route, navigation entry, and collapse behaviour.

**M9. "A single record" does not match how users think of an invoice**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L133, L150, L149, L275
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: One invoice spans document, extraction, review decision, journal entry and tax claim, so a filter on one subject misses most of its history. Decision 1's event covers several rows but has one subject. D17 makes `/documents/:id` the invoice page, so links need a document id that a journal-entry subject does not carry.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Define the subject for each event, how an invoice's full history is retrieved, and how link targets are derived.

**M10. The field boundary is not actually defined**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L89, L190-191, L231, L276-283
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction:
  - "Sensitive changes" (L190-191) has no definition or example.
  - The allowlist is never stated. Bank name, account number (treated as sensitive at L231), account type, filename and tax-claim fields are all unclassified.
  - L89 says user-entered fields are recorded, but a user's typed amendment value is not. The boundary is really by field name, not by origin.
  - "Never appear... as diffs" (L277) sits awkwardly beside naming the changed fields (L280).
- Ergonomic Requirement: Publish the allowlist per entity with three states: value shown, "changed" only, or never logged.

**M11. Credential changes are in limbo**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L187, L78, L205
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: "Login and session tokens (unless decided otherwise)" is an open question left in the non-goals. Email and password changes are real user-data writes (accounts.ex:120, :165), but they are neither covered nor excluded. Listing `hashed_password` at L78 hints at coverage.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Decide each one explicitly and delete the "unless" clause.

**M12. Balances are "diffed" but insert-only**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L96, L185-186, L282, L296-298
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: An insert has no before value. A reader cannot tell whether the row reads "Balance recorded: X" or compares with the previous snapshot.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Give the row format for insert-only events.

**M13. There is no consolidated `audit_events` shape**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L116, L122, L133-136, L265-266, L281-282, L319-320
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: Columns are scattered across sections. The format version (L136) is absent from the recommendation, Goals and Staging. It is unclear where a system actor's label lives. L265-266 keeps rejection reason apart from diffs, while L281-282 lists it as diffable.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Add one field list and resolve the rejection-reason placement.

## Nits (Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics for all)

- **N1, L310-319.** Decisions run 6, 8, 9, then 7, and criteria are numbered as a decision. Markdown will render the numbers differently from the source. Requirement: renumber in order.

It has no event catalogue, and even the row's name is contradictory (B1).

| Event kind | What the brief settles | What a reader cannot tell |
|---|---|---|
| Approve / book | Nothing specific | Whether it is one row or several; what names the invoice |
| Amend | Field names, no values (L280) | Whether booking values appear in the same row |
| Reject | Reason can be diffed (L281-282) | Whether the reason sits in `changes` or apart (L265-266) |
| Post / re-categorize | Category, need/want, notes | Tax-claim fields (status, deductible amount, tax year); the before state on first booking |
| File-reuse confirmed | Named only in staging (L342) | Whether it is covered (absent from L184-189) and what it displays |
| Upload, file replacement | "changes to documents" (L185) | Whether upload is an event; whether filename is diffed |
| Document delete | Child counts (L300) | Label, and the actor wording |
| Final extraction outcome | "error class only" (L188) | What "final" means; what success shows; what an error class looks like to a user |
| Recovery or Lifeline rescue | Named actor | Whether a rescue appears at all (M4) |
| Fingerprint backfill | Summary plus one row per document (L302-303) | Journal-entry changes; how rows collapse (B3, M6) |
| Legacy booking backfill | Not mentioned | Everything (M3) |
| Account create/update/delete | "account names" (L282) | Bank name, account number, type, currency |
| Balance snapshot | "balances" can be diffed | What a diff means for an insert-only row (M12) |
| Profile | Display name, base currency | Email and password changes (M11) |

**Does the Analysis still agree with the later decisions?** Partly. These parts no longer agree:
- §6 labels conflict with decision 2 (B1).
- §5's four job origins conflict with decision 6's three (M4).
- §1's "see Key Decisions" leads nowhere for migrations and seeds (M7).
- §7's page needs never reach Goals or Staging (M8).
- §6's format version is dropped (M13).
- §8 still talks about added columns (N2).
- The Overview still says the existing table is what gets upgraded (M1).

§2, §3 and §4 are reconciled with the decisions, apart from the stale facts in M2 and N3.

## Blockers

**B1. The entry label uses data that decision 2 bans**
- Severity: Blocker
- Location: L134-135 and L267, against L276-279; also L148 and L216
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: §6 says the write-time label is "a filename, or issuer and date", and the converging recommendation repeats the label. Decision 2 says issuer and date "never appear in the log, as values or as diffs". "Approved invoice X" (L216) and "names in place of ids" (L148) have no permitted source for X. Filename is the only surviving candidate, and decision 2's list does not mention it. It is also unclear whether the page may join the live issuer at read time. That would make a row's name change or vanish when its record is deleted.
- Ergonomic Requirement: State the exact label per subject type, and say whether read-time joins to extracted fields are allowed. Correct §6 and L267 to match.

**B2. There is no per-event definition of the page**
- Severity: Blocker
- Location: L144-153, L184-189, L274-283, L310-311
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: The page is the feature, but only its fields and filters are sketched. See the table above.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Add one table of event kinds with: trigger, actor shown, subject and label, fields shown, example row text, and link target.

**B3. "One event" is defined three incompatible ways**
- Severity: Blocker
- Location: L274-275, L302-304, L313-314, L188, L342
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction:
  - Criterion L313 requires "exactly one audit event" per covered write path.
  - Decision 5 writes 1 + N events for a backfill run.
  - L188 writes nothing for non-final extraction attempts, although each one is a write.
  - Since D17, one approve-and-book transaction writes `invoice_approved` and `journal_entry_posted`, plus `source_file_reuse_confirmed` when a reuse is confirmed. L341-342 still lists these separately, while decision 1 implies a single event.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Define the unit as the operation, list the deliberate exceptions, and state how many rows approve-and-book produces. Rewrite the criterion so it can be tested.

## Major

**M1. The Overview describes the rejected design**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L25, against L162-164, L248-251, L284-287
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: "This feature turns that table into a complete, user-readable history", but `event_logs` is frozen and replaced, with nothing copied. "Complete" also hides that the page has no pre-release history.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Rewrite L25, and specify the page's empty state or a "history starts on" notice.

**M2. Stale facts about the existing log**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L16-20, L60-61, L183; L341-342
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction:
  - L16 says four events, and L341-342 lists five. The code also has five, including `source_file_reuse_confirmed` (review.ex:402).
  - L17-20 and L60-61 call `post_entry` best-effort. It now writes its event inside the `Ecto.Multi` (accounting.ex:359), so only reject remains best-effort.
  - The reject write is at review.ex:101, not :96.
  - Goal L183, "the two paths", inherits the error.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Re-baseline these claims against the current branch.

**M3. The write-path inventory predates D17 and misses a writer**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L35, L54-55, L99-106, L184-189
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: L35 claims every write path was listed. `LegacyBookingBackfill` (/home/alexis/Development/private/zaimu-tomo/lib/zaimu_tomo/accounting/legacy_booking_backfill.ex, exposed at release.ex:41-44) is absent. It changes journal entries, writes `journal_entry_posted` events, and preserves `updated_at`. Its manual path calls `post_entry` with the entry's `user_id`, so the operator's run would look like the user's own action. The brief also never mentions D17's single booking flow.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Add this writer with a named actor, and redo the list against D17.

**M4. Actor identity is unresolved**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L118-123, L10, L305-309, L338
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction:
  - §5 lists four origins, and `initiated_by` has three values. Lifeline disappears without comment. A rescue re-runs the same job, so it would carry the original origin, but the brief never says that.
  - Key formats disagree: `system.ocr_job` against `Scope.system(:recovery)`.
  - For an upload, it is unclear whether the extraction's actor is the user or "document processing" (L10).
  - Old jobs defaulting to `upload` (L338) can misattribute recovery jobs.
  - L10 says "startup recovery", but release.ex:51 also exposes an operator-run recovery. It is unclear whether those two need different actors.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Provide a closed actor table with stable key, display label, and the rule for each origin. State that a rescue keeps the original actor, if that is the intent.

**M5. Owner of system events, and single-user versus per-user**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L65, L173, L234, against L181, L305-306, L317, L319
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: The brief argues from "single-user" but requires two-user isolation. `Scope.system(:fingerprint_backfill)` has no owner, and the backfill runs across all users. A per-run summary has no single owner, so it either leaks across users or disappears from the page.
- Ergonomic Requirement: State the tenancy model (single user in practice, per-user data model, if that is correct). Define how a system scope supplies the owner, for example one summary per affected user.

**M6. Decision 5 covers only half of the fingerprint backfill**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L41-44, L301-304, L182, L313-314
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: The backfill also sets `source_document_sha256` and `source_file_reuse_confirmed` on journal entries (fingerprint_backfill.ex:195). Decision 5 only speaks of documents. The reuse confirmation is a human decision made through a maintenance task, so its actor is unclear. A run-level summary also cannot share a transaction with row updates that commit one at a time, which conflicts with L182.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Specify the journal-entry events and the actor for confirmed reuse. Exempt the summary from the same-transaction rule explicitly, or define its transaction.

**M7. Migrations and dev seeds have no decision**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L50-56, against L299-304, L189, L313
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: L55-56 says these need explicit handling "(see Key Decisions)", but decision 5 covers only cascades and bulk updates. A silent migration is exactly the "trusted gap" L34-35 warns about.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Decide whether each is covered, excluded, or given an actor, and define "covered write path" accordingly.

**M8. §7's page requirements never become scope**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L142-153, against L180-181, L310-311, L339-340
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: Filters, keyset paging, label formatting and bulk collapse appear only as analysis. Decision 8 gives a name, but no route or navigation placement, although L142 says placement must keep the page distinct from Activity. Collapse has no run id or grouping key, and no stated default.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Move these items into Goals and specify route, navigation entry, and collapse behaviour.

**M9. "A single record" does not match how users think of an invoice**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L133, L150, L149, L275
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: One invoice spans document, extraction, review decision, journal entry and tax claim, so a filter on one subject misses most of its history. Decision 1's event covers several rows but has one subject. D17 makes `/documents/:id` the invoice page, so links need a document id that a journal-entry subject does not carry.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Define the subject for each event, how an invoice's full history is retrieved, and how link targets are derived.

**M10. The field boundary is not actually defined**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L89, L190-191, L231, L276-283
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction:
  - "Sensitive changes" (L190-191) has no definition or example.
  - The allowlist is never stated. Bank name, account number (treated as sensitive at L231), account type, filename and tax-claim fields are all unclassified.
  - L89 says user-entered fields are recorded, but a user's typed amendment value is not. The boundary is really by field name, not by origin.
  - "Never appear... as diffs" (L277) sits awkwardly beside naming the changed fields (L280).
- Ergonomic Requirement: Publish the allowlist per entity with three states: value shown, "changed" only, or never logged.

**M11. Credential changes are in limbo**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L187, L78, L205
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: "Login and session tokens (unless decided otherwise)" is an open question left in the non-goals. Email and password changes are real user-data writes (accounts.ex:120, :165), but they are neither covered nor excluded. Listing `hashed_password` at L78 hints at coverage.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Decide each one explicitly and delete the "unless" clause.

**M12. Balances are "diffed" but insert-only**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L96, L185-186, L282, L296-298
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: An insert has no before value. A reader cannot tell whether the row reads "Balance recorded: X" or compares with the previous snapshot.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Give the row format for insert-only events.

**M13. There is no consolidated `audit_events` shape**
- Severity: Major
- Location: L116, L122, L133-136, L265-266, L281-282, L319-320
- Dimension: UX & Developer Ergonomics
- Usability Friction: Columns are scattered across sections. The format version (L136) is absent from the recommendation, Goals and Staging. It is unclear where a system actor's label lives. L265-266 keeps rejection reason apart from diffs, while L281-282 lists it as diffable.
- Ergonomic Requirement: Add one field list and resolve the rejection-reason placement.
